newsitem.title: USA: Calif. bill would require review of all tax breaks.
newsitem.headline: Calif. bill would require review of all tax breaks.

text.p: A California state assemblyman has introduced legislation that would require lawmakers to conduct an evaluation of all future tax breaks, tax credits and tax exemptions, his office said on Wednesday.

Assemblyman Antonio Villaraigosa, D-Los Angeles, said Assembly Bill 559 would require future tax breaks to expire after four years unless they are subjected to the so-called "accountability evaluation."
The bill would require the state Legislative Analyst to conduct the evaluation to measure the cost efficiency and job market implications of future tax breaks.

"If the tax credit is having a positive impact, such as creating jobs, then the Legislature can confidently extend the credit at a later date," Villaraigosa said in a statement. "If it is merely a useless drain on state resources, it should simply be allowed to expire."
State officials said the measure will most likely be heard in the Assembly Revenue and Taxation Committee in early April.
